sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: And so she did.

lg.l: Why, go to then.
She that so young could give out such a seeming,
To seal her father’s eyes up close as oak,
He thought ’twas witchcraft. But I am much to blame.
I humbly do beseech you of your pardon
For too much loving you.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: I am bound to thee for ever.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: I see this hath a little dash’d your spirits.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Not a jot, not a jot.

lg.l: Trust me, I fear it has.
I hope you will consider what is spoke
Comes from my love. But I do see you’re mov’d.
I am to pray you not to strain my speech
To grosser issues nor to larger reach
Than to suspicion.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: I will not.

lg.l: Should you do so, my lord,
My speech should fall into such vile success
Which my thoughts aim’d not. Cassio’s my worthy friend.
My lord, I see you’re mov’d.
No, not much mov’d.
I do not think but Desdemona’s honest.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Long live she so! And long live you to think so!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: And yet, how nature erring from itself—

lg.l: Ay, there’s the point. As, to be bold with you,
Not to affect many proposed matches,
Of her own clime, complexion, and degree,
Whereto we see in all things nature tends;
Foh! One may smell in such a will most rank,
Foul disproportion, thoughts unnatural.
But pardon me: I do not in position
Distinctly speak of her, though I may fear
Her will, recoiling to her better judgement,
May fall to match you with her country forms,
And happily repent.
Farewell, farewell:
If more thou dost perceive, let me know more;
Set on thy wife to observe. Leave me, Iago.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Going. My lord, I take my leave.

lg.l: Why did I marry? This honest creature doubtless
Sees and knows more, much more, than he unfolds.
Returning. My lord, I would I might entreat your honour
To scan this thing no further. Leave it to time:
Though it be fit that Cassio have his place,
For sure he fills it up with great ability,
Yet if you please to hold him off awhile,
You shall by that perceive him and his means.
Note if your lady strain his entertainment
With any strong or vehement importunity,
Much will be seen in that. In the meantime,
Let me be thought too busy in my fears
(As worthy cause I have to fear I am)
And hold her free, I do beseech your honour.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Fear not my government.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: I once more take my leave.

lg.l: This fellow’s of exceeding honesty,
And knows all qualities, with a learned spirit,
Of human dealings. If I do prove her haggard,
Though that her jesses were my dear heartstrings,
I’d whistle her off, and let her down the wind
To prey at fortune. Haply, for I am black,
And have not those soft parts of conversation
That chamberers have, or for I am declin’d
Into the vale of years,—yet that’s not much—
She’s gone, I am abus’d, and my relief
Must be to loathe her. O curse of marriage,
That we can call these delicate creatures ours,
And not their appetites! I had rather be a toad,
And live upon the vapour of a dungeon,
Than keep a corner in the thing I love
For others’ uses. Yet, ’tis the plague of great ones,
Prerogativ’d are they less than the base,
’Tis destiny unshunnable, like death:
Even then this forked plague is fated to us
When we do quicken. Desdemona comes.
If she be false, O, then heaven mocks itself!
I’ll not believe’t.
How now, my dear Othello?
Your dinner, and the generous islanders
By you invited, do attend your presence.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: I am to blame.

lg.l: Why do you speak so faintly?
Are you not well?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: I have a pain upon my forehead here.

lg.l: Faith, that’s with watching, ’twill away again;
Let me but bind it hard, within this hour
It will be well.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Your napkin is too little;

div.stage: He puts the handkerchief from him, and she drops it.
div.p: Let it alone. Come, I’ll go in with you.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I am very sorry that you are not well.

lg.l: I am glad I have found this napkin;
This was her first remembrance from the Moor.
My wayward husband hath a hundred times
Woo’d me to steal it. But she so loves the token,
For he conjur’d her she should ever keep it,
That she reserves it evermore about her
To kiss and talk to. I’ll have the work ta’en out,
And give’t Iago. What he will do with it
Heaven knows, not I,
I nothing but to please his fantasy.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: How now? What do you here alone?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Do not you chide. I have a thing for you.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: A thing for me? It is a common thing—

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Ha?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: To have a foolish wife.

lg.l: O, is that all? What will you give me now
For that same handkerchief?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: What handkerchief?

lg.l: What handkerchief?
Why, that the Moor first gave to Desdemona,
That which so often you did bid me steal.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Hast stol’n it from her?

lg.l: No, faith, she let it drop by negligence,
And, to the advantage, I being here, took ’t up.
Look, here it is.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: A good wench, give it me.

lg.l: What will you do with’t, that you have been so earnest
To have me filch it?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Snatching it. Why, what’s that to you?

lg.l: If it be not for some purpose of import,
Give ’t me again. Poor lady, she’ll run mad
When she shall lack it.
Be not acknown on’t, I have use for it.
Go, leave me.

div.p: I will in Cassio’s lodging lose this napkin, And let him find it. Trifles light as air Are to the jealous confirmations strong As proofs of holy writ. This may do something. The Moor already changes with my poison: Dangerous conceits are in their natures poisons, Which at the first are scarce found to distaste, But with a little act upon the blood Burn like the mines of sulphur. I did say so.
Look, where he comes. Not poppy, nor mandragora, Nor all the drowsy syrups of the world, Shall ever medicine thee to that sweet sleep Which thou ow’dst yesterday.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Ha! ha! false to me?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Why, how now, general? No more of that.

lg.l: Avaunt! be gone! Thou hast set me on the rack.
I swear ’tis better to be much abus’d
Than but to know’t a little.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: How now, my lord?

lg.l: What sense had I of her stol’n hours of lust?
I saw’t not, thought it not, it harm’d not me.
I slept the next night well, was free and merry;
I found not Cassio’s kisses on her lips.
He that is robb’d, not wanting what is stol’n,
Let him not know’t, and he’s not robb’d at all.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: I am sorry to hear this.

lg.l: I had been happy if the general camp,
Pioners and all, had tasted her sweet body,
So I had nothing known. O, now, for ever
Farewell the tranquil mind! Farewell content!
Farewell the plumed troops and the big wars
That make ambition virtue! O, farewell,
Farewell the neighing steed and the shrill trump,
The spirit-stirring drum, the ear-piercing fife,
The royal banner, and all quality,
Pride, pomp, and circumstance of glorious war!
And, O you mortal engines, whose rude throats
The immortal Jove’s dread clamours counterfeit,
Farewell! Othello’s occupation’s gone!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Is’t possible, my lord?

lg.l: Villain, be sure thou prove my love a whore;
Be sure of it. Give me the ocular proof,
Or, by the worth of man’s eternal soul,
Thou hadst been better have been born a dog
Than answer my wak’d wrath.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Is’t come to this?

lg.l: Make me to see’t, or at the least so prove it,
That the probation bear no hinge nor loop
To hang a doubt on, or woe upon thy life!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: My noble lord,—

lg.l: If thou dost slander her and torture me,
Never pray more. Abandon all remorse;
On horror’s head horrors accumulate;
Do deeds to make heaven weep, all earth amaz’d;
For nothing canst thou to damnation add
Greater than that.
O grace! O heaven defend me!
Are you a man? Have you a soul or sense?
God be wi’ you. Take mine office.—O wretched fool,
That liv’st to make thine honesty a vice!
O monstrous world! Take note, take note, O world,
To be direct and honest is not safe.
I thank you for this profit, and from hence
I’ll love no friend, sith love breeds such offence.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Nay, stay. Thou shouldst be honest.

lg.l: I should be wise; for honesty’s a fool,
And loses that it works for.
By the world,
I think my wife be honest, and think she is not.
I think that thou art just, and think thou art not.
I’ll have some proof: her name, that was as fresh
As Dian’s visage, is now begrim’d and black
As mine own face. If there be cords or knives,
Poison or fire, or suffocating streams,
I’ll not endure ’t. Would I were satisfied!
I see, sir, you are eaten up with passion.
I do repent me that I put it to you.
You would be satisfied?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Would? Nay, I will.

lg.l: And may; but how? How satisfied, my lord?
Would you, the supervisor, grossly gape on,
Behold her topp’d?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Death and damnation! O!

lg.l: It were a tedious difficulty, I think,
To bring them to that prospect. Damn them then,
If ever mortal eyes do see them bolster
More than their own! What then? How then?
What shall I say? Where’s satisfaction?
It is impossible you should see this,
Were they as prime as goats, as hot as monkeys,
As salt as wolves in pride, and fools as gross
As ignorance made drunk. But yet I say,
If imputation and strong circumstances,
Which lead directly to the door of truth,
Will give you satisfaction, you may have’t.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Give me a living reason she’s disloyal.

lg.l: I do not like the office,
But sith I am enter’d in this cause so far,
Prick’d to ’t by foolish honesty and love,
I will go on. I lay with Cassio lately,
And being troubled with a raging tooth,
I could not sleep.
There are a kind of men so loose of soul,
That in their sleeps will mutter their affairs.
One of this kind is Cassio:
In sleep I heard him say, “Sweet Desdemona,
Let us be wary, let us hide our loves;”
And then, sir, would he gripe and wring my hand,
Cry “O sweet creature!” and then kiss me hard,
As if he pluck’d up kisses by the roots,
That grew upon my lips, then laid his leg
Over my thigh, and sigh’d and kiss’d, and then
Cried “Cursed fate that gave thee to the Moor!”

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: O monstrous! monstrous!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Nay, this was but his dream.

lg.l: But this denoted a foregone conclusion.
’Tis a shrewd doubt, though it be but a dream.
And this may help to thicken other proofs
That do demonstrate thinly.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: I’ll tear her all to pieces.

lg.l: Nay, but be wise. Yet we see nothing done,
She may be honest yet. Tell me but this,
Have you not sometimes seen a handkerchief
Spotted with strawberries in your wife’s hand?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: I gave her such a one, ’twas my first gift.

lg.l: I know not that: but such a handkerchief
(I am sure it was your wife’s) did I today
See Cassio wipe his beard with.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: If it be that,—

lg.l: If it be that, or any that was hers,
It speaks against her with the other proofs.
O, that the slave had forty thousand lives!
One is too poor, too weak for my revenge!
Now do I see ’tis true. Look here, Iago;
All my fond love thus do I blow to heaven.
’Tis gone.
Arise, black vengeance, from thy hollow hell!
Yield up, O love, thy crown and hearted throne
To tyrannous hate! Swell, bosom, with thy fraught,
For ’tis of aspics’ tongues!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Yet be content.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: O, blood, Iago, blood!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Patience, I say. Your mind perhaps may change.

lg.l: Never, Iago. Like to the Pontic Sea,
Whose icy current and compulsive course
Ne’er feels retiring ebb, but keeps due on
To the Propontic and the Hellespont;
Even so my bloody thoughts, with violent pace
Shall ne’er look back, ne’er ebb to humble love,
Till that a capable and wide revenge
Swallow them up. Now by yond marble heaven,
In the due reverence of a sacred vow Kneels.
I here engage my words.
Do not rise yet. Kneels.
Witness, you ever-burning lights above,
You elements that clip us round about,
Witness that here Iago doth give up
The execution of his wit, hands, heart,
To wrong’d Othello’s service! Let him command,
And to obey shall be in me remorse,
What bloody business ever.
I greet thy love,
Not with vain thanks, but with acceptance bounteous,
And will upon the instant put thee to ’t.
Within these three days let me hear thee say
That Cassio’s not alive.
My friend is dead. ’Tis done at your request.
But let her live.
Damn her, lewd minx! O, damn her, damn her!
Come, go with me apart, I will withdraw
To furnish me with some swift means of death
For the fair devil. Now art thou my lieutenant.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: I am your own for ever.

div.head: SCENE IV. Cyprus. Before the Castle.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Do you know, sirrah, where Lieutenant Cassio lies?

sp.speaker: CLOWN
sp.p: I dare not say he lies anywhere.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Why, man?

sp.speaker: CLOWN
sp.p: He’s a soldier; and for one to say a soldier lies is stabbing.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Go to. Where lodges he?

sp.speaker: CLOWN
sp.p: To tell you where he lodges is to tell you where I lie.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Can anything be made of this?

sp.speaker: CLOWN
sp.p: I know not where he lodges; and for me to devise a lodging, and say he lies here, or he lies there, were to lie in mine own throat.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Can you inquire him out, and be edified by report?

sp.speaker: CLOWN
sp.p: I will catechize the world for him, that is, make questions and by them answer.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Seek him, bid him come hither. Tell him I have moved my lord on his behalf, and hope all will be well.

sp.speaker: CLOWN
sp.p: To do this is within the compass of man’s wit, and therefore I will attempt the doing it.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Where should I lose that handkerchief, Emilia?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: I know not, madam.

lg.l: Believe me, I had rather have lost my purse
Full of crusadoes. And but my noble Moor
Is true of mind and made of no such baseness
As jealous creatures are, it were enough
To put him to ill thinking.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Is he not jealous?

lg.l: Who, he? I think the sun where he was born
Drew all such humours from him.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Look, where he comes.

lg.l: I will not leave him now till Cassio
Be call’d to him. How is’t with you, my lord?
Well, my good lady. Aside. O, hardness to dissemble!
How do you, Desdemona?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Well, my good lord.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Give me your hand. This hand is moist, my lady.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: It yet hath felt no age nor known no sorrow.

lg.l: This argues fruitfulness and liberal heart.
Hot, hot, and moist. This hand of yours requires
A sequester from liberty, fasting and prayer,
Much castigation, exercise devout;
For here’s a young and sweating devil here
That commonly rebels. ’Tis a good hand,
A frank one.
You may indeed say so,
For ’twas that hand that gave away my heart.
A liberal hand. The hearts of old gave hands,
But our new heraldry is hands, not hearts.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I cannot speak of this. Come now, your promise.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: What promise, chuck?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I have sent to bid Cassio come speak with you.

lg.l: I have a salt and sorry rheum offends me.
Lend me thy handkerchief.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Here, my lord.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: That which I gave you.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I have it not about me.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Not?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: No, faith, my lord.

lg.l: That is a fault. That handkerchief
Did an Egyptian to my mother give.
She was a charmer, and could almost read
The thoughts of people. She told her, while she kept it,
’Twould make her amiable and subdue my father
Entirely to her love. But if she lost it,
Or made a gift of it, my father’s eye
Should hold her loathed, and his spirits should hunt
After new fancies: she, dying, gave it me,
And bid me, when my fate would have me wive,
To give it her. I did so; and take heed on’t,
Make it a darling like your precious eye.
To lose’t or give’t away were such perdition
As nothing else could match.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Is’t possible?

lg.l: ’Tis true. There’s magic in the web of it.
A sibyl, that had number’d in the world
The sun to course two hundred compasses,
In her prophetic fury sew’d the work;
The worms were hallow’d that did breed the silk,
And it was dyed in mummy, which the skillful
Conserv’d of maiden’s hearts.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Indeed? Is’t true?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Most veritable, therefore look to ’t well.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Then would to God that I had never seen ’t!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Ha? wherefore?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Why do you speak so startingly and rash?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Is’t lost? is’t gone? speak, is it out of the way?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Heaven bless us!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Say you?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: It is not lost, but what and if it were?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: How?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I say it is not lost.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Fetch’t, let me see ’t.

lg.l: Why, so I can, sir, but I will not now.
This is a trick to put me from my suit.
Pray you, let Cassio be receiv’d again.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Fetch me the handkerchief! My mind misgives.

lg.l: Come, come.
You’ll never meet a more sufficient man.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: The handkerchief!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I pray, talk me of Cassio.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: The handkerchief!

lg.l: A man that all his time
Hath founded his good fortunes on your love,
Shar’d dangers with you,—

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: The handkerchief!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: In sooth, you are to blame.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Away!

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Is not this man jealous?

lg.l: I ne’er saw this before.
Sure there’s some wonder in this handkerchief,
I am most unhappy in the loss of it.
’Tis not a year or two shows us a man:
They are all but stomachs and we all but food;
They eat us hungerly, and when they are full,
They belch us.

div.p: Look you, Cassio and my husband.

lg.l: There is no other way; ’tis she must do ’t,
And, lo, the happiness! Go and importune her.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: How now, good Cassio, what’s the news with you?

lg.l: Madam, my former suit: I do beseech you
That by your virtuous means I may again
Exist, and be a member of his love,
Whom I, with all the office of my heart,
Entirely honour. I would not be delay’d.
If my offence be of such mortal kind
That nor my service past, nor present sorrows,
Nor purpos’d merit in futurity,
Can ransom me into his love again,
But to know so must be my benefit;
So shall I clothe me in a forc’d content,
And shut myself up in some other course
To fortune’s alms.
Alas, thrice-gentle Cassio,
My advocation is not now in tune;
My lord is not my lord; nor should I know him
Were he in favour as in humour alter’d.
So help me every spirit sanctified,
As I have spoken for you all my best,
And stood within the blank of his displeasure
For my free speech! You must awhile be patient.
What I can do I will; and more I will
Than for myself I dare. Let that suffice you.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Is my lord angry?

lg.l: He went hence but now,
And certainly in strange unquietness.
Can he be angry? I have seen the cannon,
When it hath blown his ranks into the air
And, like the devil, from his very arm
Puff’d his own brother, and can he be angry?
Something of moment then. I will go meet him.
There’s matter in’t indeed if he be angry.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I prithee do so.

div.p: Something sure of state, Either from Venice, or some unhatch’d practice Made demonstrable here in Cyprus to him, Hath puddled his clear spirit, and in such cases Men’s natures wrangle with inferior things, Though great ones are their object. ’Tis even so. For let our finger ache, and it indues Our other healthful members even to that sense Of pain. Nay, we must think men are not gods, Nor of them look for such observancy As fits the bridal. Beshrew me much, Emilia, I was (unhandsome warrior as I am) Arraigning his unkindness with my soul; But now I find I had suborn’d the witness, And he’s indicted falsely.

lg.l: Pray heaven it be state matters, as you think,
And no conception nor no jealous toy
Concerning you.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Alas the day, I never gave him cause!

lg.l: But jealous souls will not be answer’d so;
They are not ever jealous for the cause,
But jealous for they are jealous: ’tis a monster
Begot upon itself, born on itself.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Heaven keep that monster from Othello’s mind!

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Lady, amen.

lg.l: I will go seek him. Cassio, walk hereabout:
If I do find him fit, I’ll move your suit,
And seek to effect it to my uttermost.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: I humbly thank your ladyship.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Save you, friend Cassio!

lg.l: What make you from home?
How is it with you, my most fair Bianca?
I’ faith, sweet love, I was coming to your house.
And I was going to your lodging, Cassio.
What, keep a week away? Seven days and nights?
Eight score eight hours, and lovers’ absent hours,
More tedious than the dial eight score times?
O weary reckoning!
Pardon me, Bianca.
I have this while with leaden thoughts been press’d,
But I shall in a more continuate time
Strike off this score of absence. Sweet Bianca,

div.p: Take me this work out.

lg.l: O Cassio, whence came this?
This is some token from a newer friend.
To the felt absence now I feel a cause.
Is’t come to this? Well, well.
Go to, woman!
Throw your vile guesses in the devil’s teeth,
From whence you have them. You are jealous now
That this is from some mistress, some remembrance.
No, in good troth, Bianca.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Why, whose is it?

lg.l: I know not neither. I found it in my chamber.
I like the work well. Ere it be demanded,
As like enough it will, I’d have it copied.
Take it, and do ’t, and leave me for this time.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Leave you, wherefore?

lg.l: I do attend here on the general,
And think it no addition, nor my wish,
To have him see me woman’d.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Why, I pray you?

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: Not that I love you not.

lg.l: But that you do not love me.
I pray you bring me on the way a little,
And say if I shall see you soon at night.
’Tis but a little way that I can bring you,
For I attend here. But I’ll see you soon.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: ’Tis very good; I must be circumstanc’d.

div.head: ACT IV
SCENE I. Cyprus. Before the Castle.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Will you think so?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Think so, Iago?

lg.l: What,
To kiss in private?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: An unauthoriz’d kiss.

lg.l: Or to be naked with her friend in bed
An hour or more, not meaning any harm?
Naked in bed, Iago, and not mean harm?
It is hypocrisy against the devil:
They that mean virtuously and yet do so,
The devil their virtue tempts, and they tempt heaven.
So they do nothing, ’tis a venial slip.
But if I give my wife a handkerchief—

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: What then?

lg.l: Why then, ’tis hers, my lord, and being hers,
She may, I think, bestow’t on any man.
She is protectress of her honour too.
May she give that?
Her honour is an essence that’s not seen;
They have it very oft that have it not:
But for the handkerchief—
By heaven, I would most gladly have forgot it.
Thou said’st (O, it comes o’er my memory,
As doth the raven o’er the infected house,
Boding to all) he had my handkerchief.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Ay, what of that?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: That’s not so good now.

lg.l: What
If I had said I had seen him do you wrong?
Or heard him say (as knaves be such abroad,
Who having, by their own importunate suit,
Or voluntary dotage of some mistress,
Convinced or supplied them, cannot choose
But they must blab.)

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Hath he said anything?

lg.l: He hath, my lord, but be you well assur’d,
No more than he’ll unswear.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: What hath he said?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Faith, that he did—I know not what he did.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: What? What?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Lie.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: With her?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: With her, on her, what you will.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Lie with her! lie on her!—We say lie on her when they belie her.—Lie with her! that’s fulsome. Handkerchief—confessions—handkerchief! To confess, and be hanged for his labour. First, to be hanged, and then to confess. I tremble at it. Nature would not invest herself in such shadowing passion without some instruction. It is not words that shake me thus. Pish! Noses, ears, and lips. Is’t possible?—Confess?—handkerchief?—O devil!—

lg.l: Work on,
My medicine, work! Thus credulous fools are caught,
And many worthy and chaste dames even thus,
All guiltless, meet reproach. What, ho! my lord!
My lord, I say! Othello!

div.p: How now, Cassio!

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: What’s the matter?

lg.l: My lord is fallen into an epilepsy.
This is his second fit. He had one yesterday.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: Rub him about the temples.

lg.l: No, forbear;
The lethargy must have his quiet course.
If not, he foams at mouth, and by and by
Breaks out to savage madness. Look, he stirs:
Do you withdraw yourself a little while,
He will recover straight. When he is gone,
I would on great occasion speak with you.

div.p: How is it, general? Have you not hurt your head?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Dost thou mock me?

lg.l: I mock you? No, by heaven.
Would you would bear your fortune like a man!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: A horned man’s a monster and a beast.

lg.l: There’s many a beast, then, in a populous city,
And many a civil monster.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Did he confess it?

lg.l: Good sir, be a man.
Think every bearded fellow that’s but yok’d
May draw with you. There’s millions now alive
That nightly lie in those unproper beds
Which they dare swear peculiar: your case is better.
O, ’tis the spite of hell, the fiend’s arch-mock,
To lip a wanton in a secure couch,
And to suppose her chaste! No, let me know,
And knowing what I am, I know what she shall be.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: O, thou art wise, ’tis certain.

lg.l: Stand you awhile apart,
Confine yourself but in a patient list.
Whilst you were here o’erwhelmed with your grief,
(A passion most unsuiting such a man)
Cassio came hither. I shifted him away,
And laid good ’scuse upon your ecstasy,
Bade him anon return, and here speak with me,
The which he promis’d. Do but encave yourself,
And mark the fleers, the gibes, and notable scorns,
That dwell in every region of his face;
For I will make him tell the tale anew,
Where, how, how oft, how long ago, and when
He hath, and is again to cope your wife:
I say, but mark his gesture. Marry, patience,
Or I shall say you are all in all in spleen,
And nothing of a man.
Dost thou hear, Iago?
I will be found most cunning in my patience;
But,—dost thou hear?—most bloody.
That’s not amiss.
But yet keep time in all. Will you withdraw?

div.p: Now will I question Cassio of Bianca, A housewife that by selling her desires Buys herself bread and clothes: it is a creature That dotes on Cassio, (as ’tis the strumpet’s plague To beguile many and be beguil’d by one.) He, when he hears of her, cannot refrain From the excess of laughter. Here he comes.
As he shall smile Othello shall go mad, And his unbookish jealousy must construe Poor Cassio’s smiles, gestures, and light behaviour Quite in the wrong. How do you now, lieutenant?

lg.l: The worser that you give me the addition
Whose want even kills me.
Ply Desdemona well, and you are sure on’t.
Speaking lower. Now, if this suit lay in Bianca’s power,
How quickly should you speed!

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: Alas, poor caitiff!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Aside. Look how he laughs already!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: I never knew a woman love man so.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: Alas, poor rogue! I think, i’ faith, she loves me.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Aside. Now he denies it faintly and laughs it out.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Do you hear, Cassio?

lg.l: Now he importunes him
To tell it o’er. Go to, well said, well said.
She gives it out that you shall marry her.
Do you intend it?

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: Ha, ha, ha!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Do you triumph, Roman? Do you triumph?

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: I marry her? What? A customer? I prithee, bear some charity to my wit, do not think it so unwholesome. Ha, ha, ha!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: So, so, so, so. They laugh that wins.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Faith, the cry goes that you shall marry her.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: Prithee say true.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: I am a very villain else.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Have you scored me? Well.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: This is the monkey’s own giving out. She is persuaded I will marry her, out of her own love and flattery, not out of my promise.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Iago beckons me. Now he begins the story.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: She was here even now. She haunts me in every place. I was the other day talking on the sea-bank with certain Venetians, and thither comes the bauble, and falls thus about my neck.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Crying, “O dear Cassio!” as it were: his gesture imports it.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: So hangs, and lolls, and weeps upon me; so hales and pulls me. Ha, ha, ha!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Now he tells how she plucked him to my chamber. O, I see that nose of yours, but not that dog I shall throw it to.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: Well, I must leave her company.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Before me! look where she comes.

lg.l: ’Tis such another fitchew! Marry, a perfum’d one.
What do you mean by this haunting of me?

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Let the devil and his dam haunt you! What did you mean by that same handkerchief you gave me even now? I was a fine fool to take it. I must take out the work? A likely piece of work, that you should find it in your chamber and not know who left it there! This is some minx’s token, and I must take out the work? There, give it your hobby-horse. Wheresoever you had it, I’ll take out no work on’t.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: How now, my sweet Bianca? How now, how now?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: By heaven, that should be my handkerchief!

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: If you’ll come to supper tonight, you may. If you will not, come when you are next prepared for.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: After her, after her.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: Faith, I must; she’ll rail in the street else.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Will you sup there?

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: Faith, I intend so.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Well, I may chance to see you, for I would very fain speak with you.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: Prithee come, will you?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Go to; say no more.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Coming forward. How shall I murder him, Iago?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Did you perceive how he laughed at his vice?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: O Iago!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: And did you see the handkerchief?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Was that mine?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Yours, by this hand: and to see how he prizes the foolish woman your wife! she gave it him, and he hath given it his whore.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: I would have him nine years a-killing. A fine woman, a fair woman, a sweet woman!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Nay, you must forget that.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Ay, let her rot, and perish, and be damned tonight, for she shall not live. No, my heart is turned to stone; I strike it, and it hurts my hand. O, the world hath not a sweeter creature. She might lie by an emperor’s side, and command him tasks.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Nay, that’s not your way.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Hang her, I do but say what she is. So delicate with her needle, an admirable musician! O, she will sing the savageness out of a bear! Of so high and plenteous wit and invention!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: She’s the worse for all this.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: O, a thousand, a thousand times: and then of so gentle a condition!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Ay, too gentle.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Nay, that’s certain. But yet the pity of it, Iago! O Iago, the pity of it, Iago!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: If you are so fond over her iniquity, give her patent to offend, for if it touch not you, it comes near nobody.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: I will chop her into messes. Cuckold me!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: O, ’tis foul in her.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: With mine officer!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: That’s fouler.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Get me some poison, Iago; this night. I’ll not expostulate with her, lest her body and beauty unprovide my mind again. This night, Iago.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Do it not with poison, strangle her in her bed, even the bed she hath contaminated.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Good, good. The justice of it pleases. Very good.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: And for Cassio, let me be his undertaker. You shall hear more by midnight.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Excellent good. A trumpet within. What trumpet is that same?

lg.l: Something from Venice, sure. ’Tis Lodovico
Come from the duke. See, your wife is with him.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: Save you, worthy general!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: With all my heart, sir.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: The duke and senators of Venice greet you.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: I kiss the instrument of their pleasures.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: And what’s the news, good cousin Lodovico?

lg.l: I am very glad to see you, signior.
Welcome to Cyprus.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: I thank you. How does Lieutenant Cassio?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Lives, sir.

lg.l: Cousin, there’s fall’n between him and my lord
An unkind breach, but you shall make all well.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Are you sure of that?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: My lord?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Reads. “This fail you not to do, as you will—”

lg.l: He did not call; he’s busy in the paper.
Is there division ’twixt my lord and Cassio?
A most unhappy one. I would do much
To atone them, for the love I bear to Cassio.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Fire and brimstone!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: My lord?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Are you wise?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: What, is he angry?

lg.l: May be the letter mov’d him;
For, as I think, they do command him home,
Deputing Cassio in his government.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Trust me, I am glad on’t.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Indeed!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: My lord?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: I am glad to see you mad.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Why, sweet Othello?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Devil!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I have not deserv’d this.

lg.l: My lord, this would not be believ’d in Venice,
Though I should swear I saw’t: ’tis very much.
Make her amends. She weeps.
O devil, devil!
If that the earth could teem with woman’s tears,
Each drop she falls would prove a crocodile.
Out of my sight!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I will not stay to offend you.

lg.l: Truly, an obedient lady.
I do beseech your lordship, call her back.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Mistress!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: My lord?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: What would you with her, sir?

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: Who, I, my lord?

lg.l: Ay, you did wish that I would make her turn.
Sir, she can turn, and turn, and yet go on,
And turn again. And she can weep, sir, weep;
And she’s obedient, as you say, obedient,
Very obedient. Proceed you in your tears.
Concerning this, sir,—O well-painted passion!
I am commanded home.—Get you away;
I’ll send for you anon.—Sir, I obey the mandate,
And will return to Venice.—Hence, avaunt!

div.p: Cassio shall have my place. And, sir, tonight, I do entreat that we may sup together. You are welcome, sir, to Cyprus. Goats and monkeys!

lg.l: Is this the noble Moor, whom our full senate
Call all in all sufficient? Is this the nature
Whom passion could not shake? whose solid virtue
The shot of accident nor dart of chance
Could neither graze nor pierce?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: He is much chang’d.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: Are his wits safe? Is he not light of brain?

lg.l: He’s that he is. I may not breathe my censure
What he might be. If what he might he is not,
I would to heaven he were!

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: What, strike his wife?

lg.l: Faith, that was not so well; yet would I knew
That stroke would prove the worst!
Is it his use?
Or did the letters work upon his blood,
And new-create this fault?
Alas, alas!
It is not honesty in me to speak
What I have seen and known. You shall observe him,
And his own courses will denote him so
That I may save my speech: do but go after,
And mark how he continues.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: I am sorry that I am deceiv’d in him.

div.head: SCENE II. Cyprus. A Room in the Castle.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: You have seen nothing, then?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Nor ever heard, nor ever did suspect.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Yes, you have seen Cassio and she together.

lg.l: But then I saw no harm, and then I heard
Each syllable that breath made up between them.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: What, did they never whisper?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Never, my lord.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Nor send you out o’ the way?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Never.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: To fetch her fan, her gloves, her mask, nor nothing?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Never, my lord.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: That’s strange.

lg.l: I durst, my lord, to wager she is honest,
Lay down my soul at stake: if you think other,
Remove your thought, it doth abuse your bosom.
If any wretch have put this in your head,
Let heaven requite it with the serpent’s curse,
For if she be not honest, chaste, and true,
There’s no man happy. The purest of their wives
Is foul as slander.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Bid her come hither. Go.

div.p: She says enough. Yet she’s a simple bawd That cannot say as much. This is a subtle whore, A closet lock and key of villainous secrets. And yet she’ll kneel and pray. I have seen her do ’t.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: My lord, what is your will?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Pray, chuck, come hither.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: What is your pleasure?

lg.l: Let me see your eyes.
Look in my face.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: What horrible fancy’s this?

lg.l: To Emilia. Some of your function, mistress,
Leave procreants alone, and shut the door.
Cough, or cry hem, if anybody come.
Your mystery, your mystery. Nay, dispatch.
Upon my knees, what doth your speech import?
I understand a fury in your words,
But not the words.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Why, what art thou?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Your wife, my lord, your true and loyal wife.

lg.l: Come, swear it, damn thyself,
Lest, being like one of heaven, the devils themselves
Should fear to seize thee. Therefore be double-damn’d.
Swear thou art honest.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Heaven doth truly know it.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Heaven truly knows that thou art false as hell.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: To whom, my lord? With whom? How am I false?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: O Desdemona, away! away! away!

lg.l: Alas the heavy day, why do you weep?
Am I the motive of these tears, my lord?
If haply you my father do suspect
An instrument of this your calling back,
Lay not your blame on me. If you have lost him,
Why, I have lost him too.
Had it pleas’d heaven
To try me with affliction, had they rain’d
All kinds of sores and shames on my bare head,
Steep’d me in poverty to the very lips,
Given to captivity me and my utmost hopes,
I should have found in some place of my soul
A drop of patience. But, alas, to make me
A fixed figure for the time of scorn
To point his slow unmoving finger at.
Yet could I bear that too, well, very well:
But there, where I have garner’d up my heart,
Where either I must live or bear no life,
The fountain from the which my current runs,
Or else dries up, to be discarded thence,
Or keep it as a cistern for foul toads
To knot and gender in!—turn thy complexion there,
Patience, thou young and rose-lipp’d cherubin,
Ay, there, look grim as hell!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I hope my noble lord esteems me honest.

lg.l: O, ay, as summer flies are in the shambles,
That quicken even with blowing. O thou weed,
Who art so lovely fair, and smell’st so sweet,
That the sense aches at thee,
Would thou hadst ne’er been born!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Alas, what ignorant sin have I committed?

lg.l: Was this fair paper, this most goodly book,
Made to write “whore” upon? What committed?
Committed! O thou public commoner!
I should make very forges of my cheeks,
That would to cinders burn up modesty,
Did I but speak thy deeds. What committed!
Heaven stops the nose at it, and the moon winks;
The bawdy wind, that kisses all it meets,
Is hush’d within the hollow mine of earth,
And will not hear it. What committed!
Impudent strumpet!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: By heaven, you do me wrong.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Are not you a strumpet?

lg.l: No, as I am a Christian:
If to preserve this vessel for my lord
From any other foul unlawful touch
Be not to be a strumpet, I am none.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: What, not a whore?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: No, as I shall be sav’d.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Is’t possible?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: O, heaven forgive us!

lg.l: I cry you mercy then.
I took you for that cunning whore of Venice
That married with Othello.—You, mistress,

div.p: That have the office opposite to Saint Peter, And keeps the gate of hell. You, you, ay, you! We have done our course; there’s money for your pains. I pray you turn the key, and keep our counsel.

lg.l: Alas, what does this gentleman conceive?
How do you, madam? How do you, my good lady?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Faith, half asleep.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Good madam, what’s the matter with my lord?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: With who?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Why, with my lord, madam.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Who is thy lord?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: He that is yours, sweet lady.

lg.l: I have none. Do not talk to me, Emilia,
I cannot weep, nor answer have I none
But what should go by water. Prithee, tonight
Lay on my bed my wedding sheets, remember,
And call thy husband hither.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Here’s a change indeed!

lg.l: ’Tis meet I should be us’d so, very meet.
How have I been behav’d, that he might stick
The small’st opinion on my least misuse?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: What is your pleasure, madam? How is’t with you?

lg.l: I cannot tell. Those that do teach young babes
Do it with gentle means and easy tasks.
He might have chid me so, for, in good faith,
I am a child to chiding.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: What’s the matter, lady?

lg.l: Alas, Iago, my lord hath so bewhor’d her,
Thrown such despite and heavy terms upon her,
As true hearts cannot bear.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Am I that name, Iago?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: What name, fair lady?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Such as she says my lord did say I was.

lg.l: He call’d her whore: a beggar in his drink
Could not have laid such terms upon his callet.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Why did he so?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I do not know. I am sure I am none such.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Do not weep, do not weep: alas the day!

lg.l: Hath she forsook so many noble matches,
Her father, and her country, and her friends,
To be call’d whore? would it not make one weep?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: It is my wretched fortune.

lg.l: Beshrew him for’t!
How comes this trick upon him?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Nay, heaven doth know.

lg.l: I will be hang’d, if some eternal villain,
Some busy and insinuating rogue,
Some cogging, cozening slave, to get some office,
Have not devis’d this slander. I’ll be hang’d else.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Fie, there is no such man. It is impossible.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: If any such there be, heaven pardon him!

lg.l: A halter pardon him, and hell gnaw his bones!
Why should he call her whore? who keeps her company?
What place? what time? what form? what likelihood?
The Moor’s abused by some most villainous knave,
Some base notorious knave, some scurvy fellow.
O heaven, that such companions thou’dst unfold,
And put in every honest hand a whip
To lash the rascals naked through the world
Even from the east to the west!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Speak within door.

lg.l: O, fie upon them! Some such squire he was
That turn’d your wit the seamy side without,
And made you to suspect me with the Moor.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: You are a fool. Go to.

lg.l: Alas, Iago,
What shall I do to win my lord again?
Good friend, go to him. For by this light of heaven,
I know not how I lost him. Here I kneel.
If e’er my will did trespass ’gainst his love,
Either in discourse of thought or actual deed,
Or that mine eyes, mine ears, or any sense,
Delighted them in any other form,
Or that I do not yet, and ever did,
And ever will, (though he do shake me off
To beggarly divorcement) love him dearly,
Comfort forswear me! Unkindness may do much;
And his unkindness may defeat my life,
But never taint my love. I cannot say “whore,”
It does abhor me now I speak the word;
To do the act that might the addition earn
Not the world’s mass of vanity could make me.
I pray you, be content. ’Tis but his humour.
The business of the state does him offence,
And he does chide with you.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: If ’twere no other,—

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: ’Tis but so, I warrant.

div.p: Hark, how these instruments summon to supper. The messengers of Venice stay the meat. Go in, and weep not. All things shall be well.
How now, Roderigo?

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: I do not find that thou dealest justly with me.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: What in the contrary?

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: Every day thou daffest me with some device, Iago, and rather, as it seems to me now, keepest from me all conveniency than suppliest me with the least advantage of hope. I will indeed no longer endure it. Nor am I yet persuaded to put up in peace what already I have foolishly suffered.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Will you hear me, Roderigo?

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: Faith, I have heard too much, for your words and performances are no kin together.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: You charge me most unjustly.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: With naught but truth. I have wasted myself out of my means. The jewels you have had from me to deliver to Desdemona would half have corrupted a votarist: you have told me she hath received them, and returned me expectations and comforts of sudden respect and acquaintance, but I find none.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Well, go to, very well.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: Very well, go to, I cannot go to, man, nor ’tis not very well. Nay, I say ’tis very scurvy, and begin to find myself fopped in it.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Very well.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: I tell you ’tis not very well. I will make myself known to Desdemona. If she will return me my jewels, I will give over my suit and repent my unlawful solicitation. If not, assure yourself I will seek satisfaction of you.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: You have said now.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: Ay, and said nothing but what I protest intendment of doing.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Why, now I see there’s mettle in thee, and even from this instant do build on thee a better opinion than ever before. Give me thy hand, Roderigo. Thou hast taken against me a most just exception, but yet I protest, I have dealt most directly in thy affair.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: It hath not appeared.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: I grant indeed it hath not appeared, and your suspicion is not without wit and judgement. But, Roderigo, if thou hast that in thee indeed, which I have greater reason to believe now than ever,—I mean purpose, courage, and valour,—this night show it. If thou the next night following enjoy not Desdemona, take me from this world with treachery and devise engines for my life.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: Well, what is it? Is it within reason and compass?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Sir, there is especial commission come from Venice to depute Cassio in Othello’s place.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: Is that true? Why then Othello and Desdemona return again to Venice.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: O, no; he goes into Mauritania, and takes away with him the fair Desdemona, unless his abode be lingered here by some accident: wherein none can be so determinate as the removing of Cassio.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: How do you mean “removing” of him?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Why, by making him uncapable of Othello’s place: knocking out his brains.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: And that you would have me to do?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Ay, if you dare do yourself a profit and a right. He sups tonight with a harlotry, and thither will I go to him. He knows not yet of his honourable fortune. If you will watch his going thence, which I will fashion to fall out between twelve and one, you may take him at your pleasure: I will be near to second your attempt, and he shall fall between us. Come, stand not amazed at it, but go along with me. I will show you such a necessity in his death that you shall think yourself bound to put it on him. It is now high supper-time, and the night grows to waste. About it.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: I will hear further reason for this.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: And you shall be satisfied.

div.head: SCENE III. Cyprus. Another Room in the Castle.
div.stage: Enter Othello, Lodovico, Desdemona, Emilia and Attendants.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: I do beseech you, sir, trouble yourself no further.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: O, pardon me; ’twill do me good to walk.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: Madam, good night. I humbly thank your ladyship.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Your honour is most welcome.

lg.l: Will you walk, sir?—
O, Desdemona,—

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: My lord?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Get you to bed on th’ instant, I will be return’d forthwith. Dismiss your attendant there. Look ’t be done.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I will, my lord.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: How goes it now? He looks gentler than he did.

lg.l: He says he will return incontinent,
He hath commanded me to go to bed,
And bade me to dismiss you.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Dismiss me?

lg.l: It was his bidding. Therefore, good Emilia,
Give me my nightly wearing, and adieu.
We must not now displease him.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: I would you had never seen him!

lg.l: So would not I. My love doth so approve him,
That even his stubbornness, his checks, his frowns,—
Prithee, unpin me,—have grace and favour in them.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: I have laid those sheets you bade me on the bed.

lg.l: All’s one. Good faith, how foolish are our minds!
If I do die before thee, prithee, shroud me
In one of those same sheets.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Come, come, you talk.

lg.l: My mother had a maid call’d Barbary,
She was in love, and he she lov’d prov’d mad
And did forsake her. She had a song of “willow”,
An old thing ’twas, but it express’d her fortune,
And she died singing it. That song tonight
Will not go from my mind. I have much to do
But to go hang my head all at one side
And sing it like poor Barbary. Prithee dispatch.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Shall I go fetch your night-gown?

lg.l: No, unpin me here.
This Lodovico is a proper man.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: A very handsome man.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: He speaks well.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: I know a lady in Venice would have walked barefoot to Palestine for a touch of his nether lip.

lg.l: The poor soul sat sighing by a sycamore tree,
Sing all a green willow.
Her hand on her bosom, her head on her knee,
Sing willow, willow, willow.
The fresh streams ran by her, and murmur’d her moans,
Sing willow, willow, willow;
Her salt tears fell from her, and soften’d the stones;—

div.p: Lay by these:—
Prithee hie thee. He’ll come anon.

p.emph: Sing all a green willow must be my garland. Let nobody blame him, his scorn I approve,—

div.p: Nay, that’s not next. Hark! who is’t that knocks?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: It’s the wind.

lg.l: I call’d my love false love; but what said he then?
Sing willow, willow, willow:
If I court mo women, you’ll couch with mo men.

div.p: So get thee gone; good night. Mine eyes do itch; Doth that bode weeping?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: ’Tis neither here nor there.

lg.l: I have heard it said so. O, these men, these men!
Dost thou in conscience think,—tell me, Emilia,—
That there be women do abuse their husbands
In such gross kind?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: There be some such, no question.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Wouldst thou do such a deed for all the world?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Why, would not you?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: No, by this heavenly light!

lg.l: Nor I neither by this heavenly light,
I might do’t as well i’ the dark.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Wouldst thou do such a deed for all the world?

lg.l: The world’s a huge thing. It is a great price
For a small vice.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: In troth, I think thou wouldst not.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: In troth, I think I should, and undo’t when I had done. Marry, I would not do such a thing for a joint-ring, nor for measures of lawn, nor for gowns, petticoats, nor caps, nor any petty exhibition; but, for the whole world—why, who would not make her husband a cuckold to make him a monarch? I should venture purgatory for ’t.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Beshrew me, if I would do such a wrong for the whole world.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Why, the wrong is but a wrong i’ the world; and having the world for your labour, ’tis a wrong in your own world, and you might quickly make it right.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I do not think there is any such woman.

lg.l: Yes, a dozen; and as many to the vantage as would store the world they played for.
But I do think it is their husbands’ faults
If wives do fall: say that they slack their duties,
And pour our treasures into foreign laps;
Or else break out in peevish jealousies,
Throwing restraint upon us. Or say they strike us,
Or scant our former having in despite.
Why, we have galls; and though we have some grace,
Yet have we some revenge. Let husbands know
Their wives have sense like them: they see, and smell
And have their palates both for sweet and sour,
As husbands have. What is it that they do
When they change us for others? Is it sport?
I think it is. And doth affection breed it?
I think it doth. Is’t frailty that thus errs?
It is so too. And have not we affections,
Desires for sport, and frailty, as men have?
Then let them use us well: else let them know,
The ills we do, their ills instruct us so.
Good night, good night. Heaven me such usage send,
Not to pick bad from bad, but by bad mend!

div.head: ACT V
SCENE I. Cyprus. A Street.

lg.l: Here, stand behind this bulk. Straight will he come.
Wear thy good rapier bare, and put it home.
Quick, quick, fear nothing; I’ll be at thy elbow.
It makes us, or it mars us, think on that,
And fix most firm thy resolution.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: Be near at hand, I may miscarry in ’t.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Here, at thy hand. Be bold, and take thy stand.

lg.l: I have no great devotion to the deed;
And yet he hath given me satisfying reasons.
’Tis but a man gone. Forth, my sword; he dies.
I have rubb’d this young quat almost to the sense,
And he grows angry. Now, whether he kill Cassio,
Or Cassio him, or each do kill the other,
Every way makes my gain. Live Roderigo,
He calls me to a restitution large
Of gold and jewels that I bobb’d from him,
As gifts to Desdemona.
It must not be. If Cassio do remain,
He hath a daily beauty in his life
That makes me ugly. And besides, the Moor
May unfold me to him; there stand I in much peril.
No, he must die. But so, I hear him coming.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: I know his gait; ’tis he. Villain, thou diest!

div.stage: Rushes out, and makes a pass at Cassio.

lg.l: That thrust had been mine enemy indeed,
But that my coat is better than thou know’st.
I will make proof of thine.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: O, I am slain!

div.stage: Iago rushes from his post, cuts Cassio behind in the leg, and exit.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: I am maim’d forever. Help, ho! murder, murder!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: The voice of Cassio. Iago keeps his word.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: O, villain that I am!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: It is even so.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: O, help, ho! light! a surgeon!

lg.l: ’Tis he. O brave Iago, honest and just,
That hast such noble sense of thy friend’s wrong!
Thou teachest me,—minion, your dear lies dead,
And your unbless’d fate hies. Strumpet, I come!
Forth of my heart those charms, thine eyes, are blotted;
Thy bed, lust-stain’d, shall with lust’s blood be spotted.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: What, ho! No watch? No passage? murder, murder!

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: ’Tis some mischance; the cry is very direful.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: O, help!

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: Hark!

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: O wretched villain!

lg.l: Two or three groan. It is a heavy night.
These may be counterfeits. Let’s think’t unsafe
To come in to the cry without more help.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: Nobody come? Then shall I bleed to death.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: Hark!

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: Here’s one comes in his shirt, with light and weapons.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Who’s there? Whose noise is this that cries on murder?

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: We do not know.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Did not you hear a cry?

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: Here, here! for heaven’s sake, help me!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: What’s the matter?

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: This is Othello’s ancient, as I take it.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: The same indeed, a very valiant fellow.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: What are you here that cry so grievously?

lg.l: Iago? O, I am spoil’d, undone by villains!
Give me some help.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: O me, lieutenant! What villains have done this?

lg.l: I think that one of them is hereabout,
And cannot make away.
O treacherous villains!
To Lodovico and Gratiano. What are you there?
Come in and give some help.

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: O, help me here!

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: That’s one of them.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: O murderous slave! O villain!

sp.speaker: RODERIGO
sp.p: O damn’d Iago! O inhuman dog!

lg.l: Kill men i’ the dark! Where be these bloody thieves?
How silent is this town! Ho! murder! murder!
What may you be? Are you of good or evil?

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: As you shall prove us, praise us.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Signior Lodovico?

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: He, sir.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: I cry you mercy. Here’s Cassio hurt by villains.

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: Cassio!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: How is’t, brother?

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: My leg is cut in two.

lg.l: Marry, heaven forbid!
Light, gentlemen, I’ll bind it with my shirt.

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: What is the matter, ho? Who is’t that cried?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Who is’t that cried?

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: O my dear Cassio, my sweet Cassio! O Cassio, Cassio, Cassio!

lg.l: O notable strumpet! Cassio, may you suspect
Who they should be that have thus mangled you?

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: No.

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: I am sorry to find you thus; I have been to seek you.

lg.l: Lend me a garter. So.—O, for a chair,
To bear him easily hence!

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: Alas, he faints! O Cassio, Cassio, Cassio!

lg.l: Gentlemen all, I do suspect this trash
To be a party in this injury.
Patience awhile, good Cassio. Come, come;
Lend me a light. Know we this face or no?
Alas, my friend and my dear countryman
Roderigo? No. Yes, sure; O heaven! Roderigo.

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: What, of Venice?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Even he, sir. Did you know him?

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: Know him? Ay.

lg.l: Signior Gratiano? I cry you gentle pardon.
These bloody accidents must excuse my manners,
That so neglected you.

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: I am glad to see you.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: How do you, Cassio? O, a chair, a chair!

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: Roderigo!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: He, he, ’tis he.

div.p: O, that’s well said; the chair. Some good man bear him carefully from hence, I’ll fetch the general’s surgeon. To Bianca For you, mistress, Save you your labour. He that lies slain here, Cassio, Was my dear friend. What malice was between you?

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: None in the world. Nor do I know the man.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: To Bianca. What, look you pale?—O, bear him out o’ the air.

div.stage: Cassio and Roderigo are borne off.
div.p: Stay you, good gentlemen.—Look you pale, mistress? Do you perceive the gastness of her eye? Nay, if you stare, we shall hear more anon. Behold her well. I pray you, look upon her. Do you see, gentlemen? Nay, guiltiness will speak Though tongues were out of use.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: ’Las, what’s the matter? What’s the matter, husband?

lg.l: Cassio hath here been set on in the dark
By Roderigo, and fellows that are ’scap’d.
He’s almost slain, and Roderigo dead.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Alas, good gentleman! alas, good Cassio!

lg.l: This is the fruit of whoring. Prithee, Emilia,
Go know of Cassio where he supp’d tonight.
What, do you shake at that?

sp.speaker: BIANCA
sp.p: He supp’d at my house, but I therefore shake not.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: O, did he so? I charge you go with me.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Fie, fie upon thee, strumpet!

lg.l: I am no strumpet, but of life as honest
As you that thus abuse me.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: As I? Foh! fie upon thee!

lg.l: Kind gentlemen, let’s go see poor Cassio dress’d.
Come, mistress, you must tell’s another tale.
Emilia, run you to the citadel,
And tell my lord and lady what hath happ’d.
Will you go on afore? Aside. This is the night
That either makes me or fordoes me quite.

div.head: SCENE II. Cyprus. A Bedchamber in the castle.
div.stage: Desdemona in bed asleep; a light burning.

lg.l: It is the cause, it is the cause, my soul,
Let me not name it to you, you chaste stars!
It is the cause. Yet I’ll not shed her blood,
Nor scar that whiter skin of hers than snow,
And smooth as monumental alabaster.
Yet she must die, else she’ll betray more men.
Put out the light, and then put out the light:
If I quench thee, thou flaming minister,
I can again thy former light restore,
Should I repent me. But once put out thy light,
Thou cunning’st pattern of excelling nature,
I know not where is that Promethean heat
That can thy light relume. When I have pluck’d thy rose,
I cannot give it vital growth again,
It must needs wither. I’ll smell it on the tree.

div.p: O, balmy breath, that dost almost persuade Justice to break her sword! One more, one more. Be thus when thou art dead, and I will kill thee, And love thee after. One more, and this the last. So sweet was ne’er so fatal. I must weep, But they are cruel tears. This sorrow’s heavenly, It strikes where it doth love. She wakes.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Who’s there? Othello?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Ay, Desdemona.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Will you come to bed, my lord?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Have you pray’d tonight, Desdemona?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Ay, my lord.

lg.l: If you bethink yourself of any crime
Unreconcil’d as yet to heaven and grace,
Solicit for it straight.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Alack, my lord, what may you mean by that?

lg.l: Well, do it, and be brief, I will walk by.
I would not kill thy unprepared spirit,
No, heaven forfend! I would not kill thy soul.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Talk you of killing?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Ay, I do.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Then heaven have mercy on me!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Amen, with all my heart!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: If you say so, I hope you will not kill me.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Hum!

lg.l: And yet I fear you, for you are fatal then
When your eyes roll so: why I should fear I know not,
Since guiltiness I know not, but yet I feel I fear.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Think on thy sins.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: They are loves I bear to you.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Ay, and for that thou diest.

lg.l: That death’s unnatural that kills for loving.
Alas, why gnaw you so your nether lip?
Some bloody passion shakes your very frame.
These are portents; but yet I hope, I hope,
They do not point on me.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Peace, and be still!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: I will so. What’s the matter?

lg.l: That handkerchief which I so loved and gave thee,
Thou gav’st to Cassio.
No, by my life and soul!
Send for the man and ask him.
Sweet soul, take heed, take heed of perjury,
Thou’rt on thy death-bed.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Ay, but not yet to die.

lg.l: Yes, presently:
Therefore confess thee freely of thy sin.
For to deny each article with oath
Cannot remove nor choke the strong conception
That I do groan withal. Thou art to die.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Then, Lord have mercy on me!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: I say, amen.

lg.l: And have you mercy too! I never did
Offend you in my life, never lov’d Cassio
But with such general warranty of heaven
As I might love. I never gave him token.
By heaven, I saw my handkerchief in ’s hand.
O perjur’d woman, thou dost stone my heart,
And mak’st me call what I intend to do
A murder, which I thought a sacrifice.
I saw the handkerchief.
He found it then.
I never gave it him. Send for him hither.
Let him confess a truth.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: He hath confess’d.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: What, my lord?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: That he hath us’d thee.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: How? Unlawfully?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Ay.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: He will not say so.

lg.l: No, his mouth is stopp’d.
Honest Iago hath ta’en order for ’t.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: O, my fear interprets! What, is he dead?

lg.l: Had all his hairs been lives, my great revenge
Had stomach for them all.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Alas, he is betray’d, and I undone!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Out, strumpet! Weep’st thou for him to my face?

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: O, banish me, my lord, but kill me not!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Down, strumpet!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: Kill me tomorrow, let me live tonight!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Nay, if you strive,—

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: But half an hour!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Being done, there is no pause.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: But while I say one prayer!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: It is too late.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Within. My lord, my lord! what, ho! my lord, my lord!

lg.l: What noise is this? Not dead? Not yet quite dead?
I that am cruel am yet merciful,
I would not have thee linger in thy pain.
So, so.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Within. What, ho! my lord, my lord!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Who’s there?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Within. O, good my lord, I would speak a word with you!

lg.l: Yes. ’Tis Emilia, by and by. She’s dead.
’Tis like she comes to speak of Cassio’s death;
The noise was high.—Ha! no more moving?
Still as the grave. Shall she come in? Were’t good?
I think she stirs again; no. What’s best to do?
If she come in, she’ll sure speak to my wife.
My wife! my wife! what wife? I have no wife.
O, insupportable! O heavy hour!
Methinks it should be now a huge eclipse
Of sun and moon, and that the affrighted globe
Should yawn at alteration.
Within. I do beseech you
That I may speak with you, O, good my lord!
I had forgot thee: O, come in, Emilia.
Soft, by and by; let me the curtains draw.
Where art thou?

div.p: What’s the matter with thee now?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: O, my good lord, yonder’s foul murders done!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: What, now?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: But now, my lord.

lg.l: It is the very error of the moon,
She comes more nearer earth than she was wont
And makes men mad.
Cassio, my lord, hath kill’d a young Venetian
Call’d Roderigo.
Roderigo kill’d?
And Cassio kill’d?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: No, Cassio is not kill’d.

lg.l: Not Cassio kill’d! Then murder’s out of tune,
And sweet revenge grows harsh.

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: O, falsely, falsely murder’d!

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Alas, what cry is that?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: That? What?

lg.l: Out, and alas! That was my lady’s voice.
Help! help, ho! help! O lady, speak again,
Sweet Desdemona! O sweet mistress, speak!

sp.speaker: DESDEMONA
sp.p: A guiltless death I die.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: O, who hath done this deed?

lg.l: Nobody; I myself. Farewell.
Commend me to my kind lord. O, farewell!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Why, how should she be murder’d?

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Alas, who knows?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: You heard her say herself, it was not I.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: She said so. I must needs report the truth.

lg.l: She’s like a liar, gone to burning hell.
’Twas I that kill’d her.
O, the more angel she,
And you the blacker devil!

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: She turn’d to folly, and she was a whore.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Thou dost belie her, and thou art a devil.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: She was false as water.

lg.l: Thou art rash as fire, to say
That she was false: O, she was heavenly true!
Cassio did top her; ask thy husband else.
O, I were damn’d beneath all depth in hell,
But that I did proceed upon just grounds
To this extremity. Thy husband knew it all.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: My husband?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Thy husband.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: That she was false to wedlock?

lg.l: Ay, with Cassio. Nay, had she been true,
If heaven would make me such another world
Of one entire and perfect chrysolite,
I’d not have sold her for it.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: My husband?

lg.l: Ay, ’twas he that told me first.
An honest man he is, and hates the slime
That sticks on filthy deeds.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: My husband?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: What needs this iterance, woman? I say thy husband.

lg.l: O mistress, villainy hath made mocks with love!
My husband say that she was false?
He, woman;
I say thy husband: dost understand the word?
My friend, thy husband, honest, honest Iago.
If he say so, may his pernicious soul
Rot half a grain a day! he lies to the heart.
She was too fond of her most filthy bargain.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Ha!

lg.l: Do thy worst:
This deed of thine is no more worthy heaven
Than thou wast worthy her.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Peace, you were best.

lg.l: Thou hast not half that power to do me harm
As I have to be hurt. O gull! O dolt!
As ignorant as dirt! Thou hast done a deed
(I care not for thy sword) I’ll make thee known,
Though I lost twenty lives. Help! help, ho! help!
The Moor hath kill’d my mistress! Murder, murder!

sp.speaker: MONTANO
sp.p: What is the matter? How now, general?

lg.l: O, are you come, Iago? You have done well,
That men must lay their murders on your neck.

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: What is the matter?

lg.l: Disprove this villain, if thou be’st a man.
He says thou told’st him that his wife was false.
I know thou didst not, thou’rt not such a villain.
Speak, for my heart is full.
I told him what I thought, and told no more
Than what he found himself was apt and true.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: But did you ever tell him she was false?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: I did.

lg.l: You told a lie, an odious, damned lie;
Upon my soul, a lie; a wicked lie.
She false with Cassio? Did you say with Cassio?

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: With Cassio, mistress. Go to, charm your tongue.

lg.l: I will not charm my tongue; I am bound to speak.
My mistress here lies murder’d in her bed.

sp.speaker: ALL
sp.p: O heavens forfend!

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: And your reports have set the murder on.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Nay, stare not, masters, it is true indeed.

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: ’Tis a strange truth.

sp.speaker: MONTANO
sp.p: O monstrous act!

lg.l: Villany, villany, villany!
I think upon’t, I think I smell’t; O villany!
I thought so then. I’ll kill myself for grief.
O villany, villany!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: What, are you mad? I charge you, get you home.

lg.l: Good gentlemen, let me have leave to speak.
’Tis proper I obey him, but not now.
Perchance, Iago, I will ne’er go home.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: O! O! O!

lg.l: Nay, lay thee down and roar;
For thou hast kill’d the sweetest innocent
That e’er did lift up eye.
Rising. O, she was foul!
I scarce did know you, uncle, there lies your niece,
Whose breath indeed these hands have newly stopp’d.
I know this act shows horrible and grim.
Poor Desdemona! I am glad thy father’s dead.
Thy match was mortal to him, and pure grief
Shore his old thread in twain: did he live now,
This sight would make him do a desperate turn,
Yea, curse his better angel from his side,
And fall to reprobance.
’Tis pitiful. But yet Iago knows
That she with Cassio hath the act of shame
A thousand times committed; Cassio confess’d it,
And she did gratify his amorous works
With that recognizance and pledge of love
Which I first gave her; I saw it in his hand.
It was a handkerchief, an antique token
My father gave my mother.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: O heaven! O heavenly powers!

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Come, hold your peace.

lg.l: ’Twill out, ’twill out. I peace?
No, I will speak as liberal as the north.
Let heaven and men and devils, let them all,
All, all, cry shame against me, yet I’ll speak.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Be wise, and get you home.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: I will not.

div.stage: Iago offers to stab his wife.

lg.l: Fie!
Your sword upon a woman?
O thou dull Moor, that handkerchief thou speak’st of
I found by fortune and did give my husband;
For often with a solemn earnestness,
More than indeed belong’d to such a trifle,
He begg’d of me to steal it.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Villanous whore!

lg.l: She give it Cassio! no, alas, I found it,
And I did give’t my husband.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: Filth, thou liest!

lg.l: By heaven, I do not, I do not, gentlemen.
O murderous coxcomb! What should such a fool
Do with so good a wife?
Are there not stones in heaven
But what serve for thunder? Precious villain!

div.stage: Iago stabs Emilia and then runs out.

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: The woman falls. Sure, he hath kill’d his wife.

sp.speaker: EMILIA
sp.p: Ay, ay. O, lay me by my mistress’ side.

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: He’s gone, but his wife’s kill’d.

lg.l: ’Tis a notorious villain. Take you this weapon,
Which I have here recover’d from the Moor.
Come, guard the door without, let him not pass,
But kill him rather. I’ll after that same villain,
For ’tis a damned slave.
I am not valiant neither,
But every puny whipster gets my sword.
But why should honour outlive honesty?
Let it go all.
What did thy song bode, lady?
Hark, canst thou hear me? I will play the swan,
And die in music.
Moor, she was chaste. She lov’d thee, cruel Moor,
So come my soul to bliss, as I speak true;
So speaking as I think, I die, I die.
I have another weapon in this chamber,
It is a sword of Spain, the ice-brook’s temper.
O, here it is. Uncle, I must come forth.
Within. If thou attempt it, it will cost thee dear;
Thou hast no weapon, and perforce must suffer.
Look in upon me then, and speak with me,
Or, naked as I am, I will assault thee.

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: What is the matter?

lg.l: Behold, I have a weapon.
A better never did itself sustain
Upon a soldier’s thigh: I have seen the day
That with this little arm and this good sword
I have made my way through more impediments
Than twenty times your stop. But, O vain boast!
Who can control his fate? ’Tis not so now.
Be not afraid, though you do see me weapon’d.
Here is my journey’s end, here is my butt,
And very sea-mark of my utmost sail.
Do you go back dismay’d? ’Tis a lost fear.
Man but a rush against Othello’s breast,
And he retires. Where should Othello go?
Now, how dost thou look now? O ill-starr’d wench,
Pale as thy smock, when we shall meet at compt,
This look of thine will hurl my soul from heaven,
And fiends will snatch at it. Cold, cold, my girl!
Even like thy chastity.
O cursed, cursed slave! Whip me, ye devils,
From the possession of this heavenly sight!
Blow me about in winds, roast me in sulphur,
Wash me in steep-down gulfs of liquid fire!
O Desdemon! Dead, Desdemon! dead! Oh, oh!

div.stage: Enter Lodovico, Montano, Cassio carried in a chair, and Officers with Iago prisoner.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: Where is this rash and most unfortunate man?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: That’s he that was Othello. Here I am.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: Where is that viper? Bring the villain forth.

lg.l: I look down towards his feet; but that’s a fable.
If that thou be’st a devil, I cannot kill thee.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: Wrench his sword from him.

sp.speaker: IAGO
sp.p: I bleed, sir, but not kill’d.

lg.l: I am not sorry neither. I’d have thee live,
For in my sense ’tis happiness to die.
O thou Othello, that wert once so good,
Fall’n in the practice of a damned slave,
What shall be said to thee?
Why, anything;
An honourable murderer, if you will.
For naught did I in hate, but all in honour.
This wretch hath part confess’d his villany.
Did you and he consent in Cassio’s death?

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Ay.

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: Dear general, I never gave you cause.

lg.l: I do believe it, and I ask your pardon.
Will you, I pray, demand that demi-devil
Why he hath thus ensnar’d my soul and body?
Demand me nothing. What you know, you know.
From this time forth I never will speak word.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: What, not to pray?

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: Torments will ope your lips.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: Well, thou dost best.

lg.l: Sir, you shall understand what hath befall’n,
Which, as I think, you know not. Here is a letter
Found in the pocket of the slain Roderigo,
And here another. The one of them imports
The death of Cassio, to be undertook
By Roderigo.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: O villain!

sp.speaker: CASSIO
sp.p: Most heathenish and most gross!

lg.l: Now here’s another discontented paper,
Found in his pocket too; and this, it seems,
Roderigo meant to have sent this damned villain,
But that, belike, Iago in the interim
Came in and satisfied him.
O the pernicious caitiff!
How came you, Cassio, by that handkerchief
That was my wife’s?
I found it in my chamber.
And he himself confess’d but even now,
That there he dropp’d it for a special purpose
Which wrought to his desire.

sp.speaker: OTHELLO
sp.p: O fool! fool! fool!

lg.l: There is besides in Roderigo’s letter,
How he upbraids Iago, that he made him
Brave me upon the watch, whereon it came
That I was cast. And even but now he spake,
After long seeming dead, Iago hurt him,
Iago set him on.
You must forsake this room, and go with us.
Your power and your command is taken off,
And Cassio rules in Cyprus. For this slave,
If there be any cunning cruelty
That can torment him much and hold him long,
It shall be his. You shall close prisoner rest,
Till that the nature of your fault be known
To the Venetian state. Come, bring away.
Soft you; a word or two before you go.
I have done the state some service, and they know’t.
No more of that. I pray you, in your letters,
When you shall these unlucky deeds relate,
Speak of me as I am. Nothing extenuate,
Nor set down aught in malice. Then must you speak
Of one that loved not wisely, but too well;
Of one not easily jealous, but being wrought,
Perplex’d in the extreme; of one whose hand,
Like the base Judean, threw a pearl away
Richer than all his tribe; of one whose subdu’d eyes,
Albeit unused to the melting mood,
Drop tears as fast as the Arabian trees
Their medicinal gum. Set you down this.
And say besides, that in Aleppo once,
Where a malignant and a turban’d Turk
Beat a Venetian and traduc’d the state,
I took by the throat the circumcised dog,
And smote him, thus.

sp.speaker: LODOVICO
sp.p: O bloody period!

sp.speaker: GRATIANO
sp.p: All that’s spoke is marr’d.

lg.l: I kiss’d thee ere I kill’d thee. No way but this,
Killing myself, to die upon a kiss.
This did I fear, but thought he had no weapon,
For he was great of heart.
To Iago. O Spartan dog,
More fell than anguish, hunger, or the sea,
Look on the tragic loading of this bed.
This is thy work. The object poisons sight,
Let it be hid. Gratiano, keep the house,
And seize upon the fortunes of the Moor,
For they succeed on you. To you, lord governor,
Remains the censure of this hellish villain.
The time, the place, the torture, O, enforce it!
Myself will straight aboard, and to the state
This heavy act with heavy heart relate.
